title: Rabbi Abba bar Ada
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 4:6 relates that his maidservant fled to Kilisiya. He consulted Rabbi Mani, who ruled like Rabbi Immi. That is, he lived in the Land of Israel and she fled abroad; he asked whether he could sell her. Hyman identifies this as the later Rabbi Mana. He therefore distinguishes the subject from Rabbi Abba bar Rav Ada, who reports Rabbi Yitzchak in Shabbat 130a, where Rav Yosef challenges the teaching. In particular, Dikdukei Soferim reads Ravin bar Ada there; see that entry.

notes.text: Kilisiya is retained without a new geographical or ecclesiastical identification. The later Mana and the different Abba/Ravin traditions are Hyman’s distinctions.
